input:
If the function f(x) is continuous in 0 ≤ x ≤ π, then the value of 2a + 3b is where
f(x) = { x + a√2 sin x,       if 0 ≤ x < π/4
        { 2x cot x + b,       if π/4 ≤ x ≤ π/2
        { a cos 2x - b sin x, if π/2 < x ≤ π }

Options:
A. π/12
B. π/6
C. π/4
D. π/10

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Find constants a and b such that the piecewise function f(x) is continuous at the transition points x = π/4 and x = π/2, then compute 2a + 3b.

given_information.f_piece_1: x + a√2 sin x  for 0 ≤ x < π/4
given_information.f_piece_2: 2x cot x + b   for π/4 ≤ x ≤ π/2
given_information.f_piece_3: a cos 2x - b sin x  for π/2 < x ≤ π

phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: Continuity requires matching left-hand and right-hand limits at both x = π/4 and x = π/2. This gives two equations in a and b, which can be solved simultaneously.

key_concepts: Trigonometric values at π/4 and π/2

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Apply continuity at x = π/4 (equate piece 1 limit and piece 2 value) and at x = π/2 (equate piece 2 limit and piece 3 limit) to get two linear equations; solve for a and b; compute 2a + 3b.
logical_steps: Step 1: Apply continuity at x = π/4 using piece 1 and piece 2
Step 2: Simplify to get equation (i): a - b = π/4
Step 3: Apply continuity at x = π/2 using piece 2 and piece 3
Step 4: Simplify to get equation (ii): a = -2b
Step 5: Substitute (ii) into (i) and solve for b, then a

step_3_continuity_at_pi_over_2.LHL: lim(x→π/2⁻) (2x cot x + b) = 2(π/2)·cot(π/2) + b = π·0 + b = b
step_3_continuity_at_pi_over_2.RHL: lim(x→π/2⁺) (a cos 2x - b sin x) = a cos(π) - b sin(π/2) = a(-1) - b(1) = -a - b
